meta.note: Every capability in this physical-intelligence stack has two dates: the year it first worked, and the year it arrived in volume. The distance between them is the lag. Bars are laid out by stratum, so the chart reads top-to-bottom as the stack reads — ore at the top of the list, autonomous physical work at the bottom.

definitions.invented: The year the capability was first demonstrated in a lab, patent, or working prototype.
definitions.shipped: The year it reached high-volume industrial deployment or commercial series production.
definitions.lag: shipped − invented. Where an entry has not shipped, it has no lag.

confidence.label: Dated
confidence.note: Both years are documented and verified in technical literature. Argue about a year either way, not a decade.

confidence.label: Contested
confidence.note: One date is an editorial judgement call depending on volume thresholds. The bar is right to within a few years.

confidence.label: Not shipped
confidence.note: Early lab prototype or pilot testing; volume production date unconfirmed.

waitedFor.label: The science
waitedFor.note: Kinematics, dynamics, contact mechanics, or materials physics were genuinely incomplete.

waitedFor.label: A machine
waitedFor.note: Machine tools, sub-micron grinding, or semiconductor lithography were missing.

waitedFor.label: A better reason
waitedFor.note: Incumbent manual labor or hydraulic machinery was cheaper until conditions changed.

waitedFor.label: Something to run on
waitedFor.note: Required GPU compute, high-frequency bus bandwidth, or fleet scale.

waitedFor.label: Someone to want it
waitedFor.note: Technology worked, but broad industrial demand took decades to develop.

events.label: Bastnäsite rare earth flotation
events.note: Ding Daoheng discovered the Bayan Obo deposit in 1927. Industrial foam flotation and chemical beneficiation methods took thirty-one years to scale to volume.

source.what: Geological History of Bayan Obo Deposit

events.label: Hard-rock lithium pyrometallurgy
events.note: Acid-roasting of alpha-to-beta spodumene concentrate was perfected in 1950. Sat until commercial grease and glass ceramics created stable industrial demand.

events.label: Sintered NdFeB permanent magnets
events.note: Masato Sagawa (Sumitomo) and John Croat (General Motors) developed Nd₂Fe₁₄B in 1982, quadrupling motor torque density over ferrite within seven years.

source.what: IEEE Milestone in Nd-Fe-B Permanent Magnets

events.label: Electro-slag remelted 100Cr6 steel
events.note: R.K. Hopkins patented consumable-electrode ESR in 1940. Adopted by precision bearing foundries in 1965 to eliminate non-metallic micro-inclusions.

events.label: Gel-spun UHMWPE tendon fiber
events.note: Pennings and Smith discovered ultra-drawn gel-spinning of ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene in 1963. DSM commercialized Dyneema in 1990.

events.label: Non-grain-oriented electrical steel
events.note: Goss patented electrical silicon steel in 1934. Non-oriented isotropic laminations were scaled in 1955 for high-efficiency rotary motor stators.

source.what: History of Electrical Steel Sheet Development

events.label: 5-axis CNC continuous path grinding
events.note: Sub-micron optical scale closed-loop feedback on CNC machine tools enabled continuous grinding of conjugate tooth profiles for harmonic reducers.

events.label: PCBN hard turning of bearing rings
events.note: Polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PCBN) cutting inserts enabled direct hard turning of hardened 62 HRC bearing raceways without rough grinding.

events.label: Crossed-roller pivot bearing
events.note: THK and IKO introduced crossed-roller bearings in the 1960s, replacing dual tapered roller sets with a single compact joint pivot ring.

source.what: Pioneering Linear Motion and Crossed Roller Bearings

events.label: Planetary roller screw
events.note: Carl Bruno Strandgren patented the planetary roller screw in 1954. Remained an aerospace specialty until robotics required high-load linear actuators.

events.label: RV cycloidal speed reducer
events.note: Lorenz Braren patented the cycloidal speed reducer in 1926. Nabtesco mastered sub-micron pin-wheel grinding in 1985, anchoring heavy robot base joints.

events.label: Strain-wave gearing (Harmonic Drive)
events.note: C. Walton Musser invented strain-wave gearing in 1955. Aerospace and industrial robot joints adopted it for zero-backlash high-ratio reduction.

events.label: Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD) actuators
events.note: Wensing et al. at MIT proved high-torque-density motors with low-ratio (<10:1) planetary gearing enable dynamic proprioceptive legged locomotion.

source.what: Proprioceptive Actuator Design in the MIT Cheetah, 2017

events.label: Frameless direct-drive BLDC motor
events.note: T.G. Wilson patented electronic commutated DC motors in 1962. Kollmorgen and Parker put frameless rotor-stator kits into volume robotic joints in 1984.

source.what: D.C. Machine with Solid State Commutation, 1962

events.label: Dual-rotor axial-flux torque motor
events.note: Faraday built the first axial disc dynamo in 1831. High-coercivity magnets and PCB stator fabrication in 2021 unlocked unmatched torque density for joint modules.

source.what: Axial flux permanent magnet machine development

events.label: Integrated smart robotic joint module
events.note: DLR developed the modular LWR joint in 2008. Universal Robots and Robotiq commercialized all-in-one cylindrical joint actuators with onboard DSP drivers.

events.label: Series Elastic Actuation (SEA)
events.note: Pratt and Williamson introduced mechanical elasticity between motor and load in 1995. Rethink Robotics (Baxter) put SEAs into series cobot production in 2012.

events.label: Optical absolute multi-turn encoder
events.note: Heidenhain and Tamagawa developed multi-track glass code discs in 1958, reaching 24-bit single-turn resolution in volume robot joints by 1982.

events.label: Monolithic magnetic angle sensor
events.note: Edwin Hall discovered the Hall effect in 1879. Silicon CMOS integration of differential Hall arrays in 1998 enabled dirt-immune 14-bit magnetic joint encoders.

events.label: GelSight optical elastomeric skin
events.note: Adelson's lab at MIT used elastomeric gel and photometric stereo in 2009. Commercialized in 2021 for high-resolution robotic fingertip tactile sensing.

source.what: Retrographic Sensing for the Measurement of Surface Texture, 2009

events.label: Solid-state flash time-of-flight LiDAR
events.note: Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) CMOS receiver arrays replaced spinning mirrors, enabling miniature 3D range cameras on robots.

events.label: Neuromorphic event-based vision
events.note: Lichtsteiner and Delbruck built the Dynamic Vision Sensor (DVS) in 2008. Reached megapixel production in 2024 for microsecond-latency robot obstacle reaction.

source.what: A 128x128 120 dB 15 us Latency Asynchronous Temporal Contrast Vision Sensor, 2008

events.label: Embedded robotics AI processor
events.note: NVIDIA Xavier/Orin integrated multi-core ARM, GPU tensor cores, and hardware vision accelerators into a 40W SoC executing real-time deep neural policies onboard.

events.label: High-rate LiFePO4 battery pack
events.note: Goodenough discovered LiFePO4 in 1997. Carbon-coating and cell engineering enabled 20C peak pulse discharge required for dynamic jumping and heavy manipulator lifts.

source.who: Padhi, Nanjundaswamy, Goodenough, J. Electrochem. Soc.

events.label: GaN high-frequency joint inverter
events.note: Efficient Power Conversion (EPC) commercialized enhancement-mode GaN-on-Si. Switching at 100 kHz eliminated bulk electrolytic capacitors in joint motor drivers.

events.label: Anthropomorphic 5-finger robot hand
events.note: Jacobsen developed the Utah/MIT Dextrous Hand in 1983. Took forty-one years of tendon, motor, and tactile sensor miniaturization to produce robust commercial hands.

source.what: The Utah/MIT Dextrous Hand: Work in Progress, 1984

events.label: Laser tracker volumetric calibration
events.note: Lau and Hocken patented 6-DOF laser tracking interferometry in 1986. Commercialized in 1999 by Leica/API to calibrate Denavit-Hartenberg parameters down to 20 µm.

events.label: Field-Oriented Vector Control (FOC)
events.note: Felix Blaschke (Siemens) formulated vector control in 1971. Required fast digital signal processors (DSPs) before shipping in volume motor drives.

events.label: Deterministic EtherCAT fieldbus
events.note: Beckhoff Automation introduced EtherCAT in 2003. Delivered 100 Mbps sub-microsecond jitter synchronization across 100+ joint axes.

events.label: Robot Operating System (ROS / ROS 2)
events.note: Willow Garage created ROS in 2007. ROS 2 migrated to deterministic DDS transport in 2018, becoming the universal open middleware standard across 1,000+ robot platforms.

source.what: ROS 2 Bouncy Bolson release and DDS standard

events.label: Whole-Body Dynamic Control (WBC)
events.note: Oussama Khatib proposed operational space dynamic control in 1987. Scaled to real-time quadratic programming solvers running at 1 kHz on Boston Dynamics Atlas in 2015.

source.what: A Unified Approach for Motion and Force Control of Robot Manipulators, 1987

events.label: Cartesian Impedance Control
events.note: Neville Hogan formulated impedance control in 1985. Commercialized in DLR/KUKA LBR iiwa in 2008, enabling safe physical human-robot contact without rigid jamming.

source.what: Impedance Control: An Approach to Manipulation, 1985

events.label: Low-cost bimanual teleoperation (ALOHA)
events.note: Goertz built master-slave teleoperators at Argonne in 1954. Stanford's ALOHA democratized bilateral teleoperation data collection at 100x lower cost in 2023.

source.what: Learning Fine Collaborative Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware, 2023

events.label: MuJoCo contact physics engine
events.note: Emo Todorov formulated convex optimization contact physics in 2012. Became the universal foundation for robotic reinforcement learning and policy benchmarking.

source.what: MuJoCo: A Physics Engine for Model-Based Control, 2012

events.label: Massively parallel GPU simulation
events.note: Liang et al. and NVIDIA Isaac Gym simulated 10,000+ robots in parallel on a single GPU in 2018, reducing months of locomotion training to twenty minutes.

source.what: Isaac Gym: High Performance GPU-Based Physics Simulation for Robot Learning, 2021

events.label: Diffusion Policy for robotic manipulation
events.note: Chi et al. adapted generative diffusion models to represent multimodal visuomotor action distributions, eliminating compounding errors in complex manipulation tasks.

source.what: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion, 2023

events.label: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models
events.note: RT-2, Octo, and OpenVLA merged internet-scale multimodal LLMs directly with low-level robot joint action tokenizers, enabling open-world instruction following.

source.who: Brohan et al., CoRL / Google DeepMind
source.what: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control, 2023

events.label: Hardware-in-the-loop dynamic dyno assay
events.note: Multi-axis motorized dyno testbenches simulate real-world inertial and thermal shock loads, qualifying joint lifetime to 20,000 hours before deployment.

source.what: ISO 9283 Performance Criteria for Manipulating Industrial Robots

events.label: Hierarchical Task & Motion Planning (TAMP)
events.note: STRIPS and Shakey introduced symbolic planning in 1971. Integrating continuous trajectory optimization with discrete logic search took four decades of compute advances.

source.what: STRIPS: A New Approach to the Application of Theorem Proving to Problem Solving, 1971

events.label: Decentralized warehouse AMR fleet dispatch
events.note: Mick Mountz founded Kiva Systems in 2003. Amazon acquired Kiva in 2012 and deployed 500,000+ mobile drive units under automated grid scheduling.

source.what: Coordinating Hundreds of Cooperative, Autonomous Vehicles in Warehouses, 2008

events.label: The industrial robot arm (Unimate)
events.note: George Devol patented programmed article transfer in 1954; Joseph Engelberger commercialized Unimate at GM Trenton die-casting in 1961.

events.label: Lightweight collaborative robot (UR5)
events.note: Esben Østergaard founded Universal Robots in 2008. Shipped the UR5 in 2011, eliminating perimeter safety cages and creating the collaborative robotics category.

events.label: Safety optical area scanner (ISO 13849)
events.note: SICK and Keyence developed dual-microprocessor laser scanners with muting zones, certifying collaborative cell perimeter safety to SIL 3 / PLd.

source.what: History of Industrial Safety Laser Scanners

events.label: Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) capital model
events.note: Transformed high upfront capex into opex hourly billing tied to pick rate, accelerating adoption across warehouse intralogistics fleets.

events.label: Hydrogen decrepitation magnet recycling
events.note: Hydrogen decrepitation breaks end-of-life sintered NdFeB motor magnets back into sub-micron powder without chemical dissolution, saving 90% embodied energy.
